figures.caption: Figure 1: YOLOv14 system pipeline. The architecture comprises six stages: scene analysis, adaptive augmentation (training-only), Game2Real domain adaptation via AdaIN and adversarial loss, multi-view conditioning through ViewEmbedding, deformable feature pyramid with DynamicScaleRouter, and multi-scale detection heads.

Table 2: Comprehensive comparison with state-of-the-art real-time detectors on COCO val2017. All metrics measured on T4 TensorRT FP16 (batch=1, imgsz=640) unless noted. †Estimated from official checkpoints. All YOLOv14 results are mean ± std over 3 runs.
Table 3: Ablation study. Each row adds a component to the YOLOv12s baseline. COCO column reports mean ± std over 3 runs.

Figure 2: Qualitative detection results across challenging scenarios. The figure presents five representative examples arranged in two rows: top row (a)–(c) shows (a) persons near boundaries in a strongly distorted fisheye image, (b) game characters in a Delta-Force-style scene detected as person, and (c) small vehicles from an aerial drone perspective; bottom row (d)–(e) shows (d) objects in a pinhole street-view image, and (e) objects across a 360◦ equirectangular panorama.

Figure 3: Latency-accuracy trade-off on COCO val2017. YOLOv14 (red stars) consistently outperforms prior detectors across all model scales. The dashed red line shows the YOLOv14 Pareto frontier.
